title: Penguin Poop is Melting Antarctic Snow - Nautilus
author: Devin Reese
text:
Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentPenguin Poop is Melting Antarctic SnowThanks to green algae that groove on guanoDRBy Devin Reese8:00 AM CDT on October 7, 2026Add Nautilus to GooglePenguin in a zoo standing alone in snow during falling snow, lifting his tail up to take a leak
Penguins are messy, gathering in dense huddles where their guano (aka poop) piles up on the ice. In fact, their poop piles are so dense that they show up on satellite images. And the guano stains aren’t just in the spots where penguins let loose their bowels, but also where they track it when they waddle around on the snow. Moreover, a new study published today in the Journal of Geophysical Research Biogeosciences found that penguin guano has far-reaching impacts on the Antarctic landscape by nourishing snow algae that grow on the surface.The study authors traveled through the blustery Drake Passage that links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans to reach the West Antarctic Peninsula, where they gathered samples of snow algae, some of which appears red and some of which appears green. Back in the lab, they extracted pigments and nutrients from each sample. The green samples proved richer in phosphate, which comes from penguin guano. It allows algae to load their cells with chlorophyll and boost photosynthesis. In contrast, the red algae were low in phosphate and instead derived their color from red pigments, which act as sunscreen when they go inactive during times of nutrient scarcity.  Read more: “What Satellite Photos of Penguin Poop Tell Us About Earth’s Health”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
